nodes.name: Agent-Substrate-Autonomy Proposal
nodes.summary: Identifies the gap between the current agent-tool invocation model (conservative SKILL, reactive policy) and the memory-centric vision where HipCortex substrate acts as the primary cognitive mind. Proposes a proactive SKILL harness, engine defaults for AgentMessage paths, a unified get_live_beliefs surface, and validated 80-99% LLM token reduction benchmarks.

nodes.name: Agent-Substrate-Autonomy Design
nodes.summary: Resolves all five open threads (token math, beliefs merge, compliance, layering, multi-agent) with code-grounded evidence. Defines eight key design decisions including policy-first approach, opt-in engine defaults for AgentMessage, unified beliefs surface merging symbolic+hypotheses+world+intel, and validation via extended benchmarks targeting 80%+ reduction.

nodes.name: Agent-Substrate-Autonomy Tasks
nodes.summary: Four-phase task breakdown: Phase 1 updates the Python SKILL template and CLI installer for proactive/substrate-first mode; Phase 2 wires PerceptionSession defaults and get_live_beliefs in Rust; Phase 3 formalizes multi-agent actor scoping and docs; Phase 4 extends benchmarks and validates 80%+ token reduction. All tasks include explicit verification criteria.
